newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary owes Croatia $1 mln in arms deal - lawyer.
newsitem.headline: Hungary owes Croatia $1 mln in arms deal - lawyer.

text.p: Hungary owes neighbouring Croatia a $1 million refund for Kalashnikov automatic rifles bought in 1990, some of which were never delivered because of publicity about the deal just before the Croatian war, a lawyer said on Friday.

Hungarian lawyer Tamas Elter said he had filed a claim with Hungary's privatisation agency APV Rt on behalf of the Croatian government in an effort to end a long dispute over the arms shipment that prompted a major scandal in Hungary.

Hungary acknowledged in 1990 that it had sent 10,000 AK-47 rifles to Croatian separatists, but then prime minister Jozsef Antall stopped further supplies and sent an envoy to Belgrade to smoothe relations.
"Croatia raised the issue in 1991 and was given many promises by APV and by the Hungarian government," Elter told Reuters.
"Within APV there were two views -- one that this is just a business deal and the other concerned about the political implications," Elter added.

Elter said Croatia's most recent claim against Hungary sought a refund of $985,000, plus interest, for money that was transferred to Hungary's Technika Foreign Trading Company by Freeburn Company Ltd, acting for the Croatian government.
The Hungarian trading company later came under the control of APV and has since been liquidated, but Elter said the liquidator had agreed the claim was valid.
Asked where he thought the money might be, Elter said, "That is a question I can't answer."
Officials at APV were not available for comment.
